title: SLO Workshop Playbook for Feature Owners & Customer Success
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a lightweight, practical facilitator guide and checklist to run 30/60/90-day SLO adoption workshops with feature owners and customer success partners. The goal is to convert product-level reliability objectives into measurable SLOs, owner commitments, and an operational runbook that fits into the team's existing cadence.

Assumptions and audience:
- Audience: feature/product owners, engineering leads, CS/Customer Success managers, oncall reps, and an SRE facilitator.
- Teams have a basic telemetry feed into our observability stack (request counts, latencies, error rates).
- This is for teams adopting service-level SLOs that map to customer-facing user journeys (not infra-only internal services).

High-level outcomes for a 90-day adoption: 
- 30 days: establish one working SLO, monitoring dashboard, and a simple alert/incident trigger.
- 60 days: refine SLO targets, add error budget policy and escalation path, and run two tabletop simulations.
- 90 days: productionize rollout (canary + full), integrate SLOs into release checklist, and document postmortem expectations.

Workshop format (90 minutes for kickoff):
1) 0–10 min (Context): quick framing: why SLOs vs. raw alerts, ties to customer impact, and success criteria for this workshop.
2) 10–25 min (Map the user journey): product owner sketches primary happy path and failure scenarios (done on a whiteboard or Miro). Capture key steps where latency/errors impact customer value.
3) 25–40 min (Choose SLI candidates): SRE facilitator proposes 3 candidate SLIs drawn from existing telemetry (p95 latency, error-rate for key endpoint, successful completion ratio). Quick pros/cons.
4) 40–55 min (Set initial targets): pick a conservative target for the first SLO (e.g., p95 < 250ms 99.5% of the time OR availability 99.9% for critical flows). If metrics are immature, pick an instrumented monitoring target instead and a measurement plan.
5) 55–75 min (Runbook sketch and error budget policy): define what happens when error budget is exhausted, who stops new feature releases, and escalation owners.
6) 75–90 min (Next steps & owners): decide immediate deliverables for the 30-day window and assign owners.

Templates and artifacts produced during the workshop (minimum deliverables):
- SLO one-pager: short description, SLI definition (query + unit), SLO target, measurement window, and business rationale.
- Dashboard template: graphs for SLI, burn rate, and request volume.
- Incident play snippet: what to look for when burn rate spikes > 3x and who to call.
- Measurement checklist: data quality checks and data-smoothing rules.

Example SLO one-pager (copyable):
Title: Search API - Query Completion SLO
SLI definition: fraction of successful query completions (status = 200 and payload.size > 0) per 1m window
Query example (PromQL-ish): sum(successful_query_count{route="search"}) / sum(total_query_count{route="search"})
Target: 99.5% over a rolling 7d window
Burn policy: if burn rate > 2 for 2 consecutive 1h windows, page SRE on-call and pause non-critical releases.
Business rationale: Search directly affects conversion; small availability regressions materially impact revenue.
Owner: Feature Owner + Backend Lead

Measurement & instrumentation checklist (practical):
- Confirm unique request id flows through proxy -> service -> telemetry pipeline.
- Verify telemetry cardinality (route tag present, user_type if needed).
- Check for sampling; ensure SLI uses unsampled counts OR an aggregation compensated for sampling.
- Add a fallback metric for degraded telemetry (e.g., synthetic probe) if your production signal is sparse.

30/60/90 milestone plan (what to deliver):
30-day sprint (owner: Feature Owner):
- Deliver SLO one-pager (owner: Feature Owner)
- Basic dashboard in the shared SRE folder (owner: Observability Engineer)
- One-run tabletop postmortem simulation scheduled and executed (owner: SRE facilitator)

60-day sprint (owner: Engineering Lead):
- Implement error budget alerting thresholds and automation (owner: Platform/Observability)
- Capture runbook steps in Ops Runbook (owner: Engineering Manager)
- Complete two incident drills and record improvements (owner: CS lead + SRE)

90-day sprint (owner: Product Manager):
- Canary rollout gates integrated with burn-rate check (owner: Release Engineering)
- SLO included in PR checklist for changes that touch the critical path (owner: Developer Experience)
- Finalize post-adoption retrospective and signoff (owner: Product Manager)

Comms and stakeholder cadence:
- Weekly SLO sync for first 30 days (15 min) — owner status, telemetry health, blockers.
- Monthly reliability review board for stakeholders — burn rate trends, regressions, and roadmap changes.
- Customer Success: add CS to monthly review; share SLO health in customer-facing status updates when relevant.

Risk register (short):
- Measurement risk: metric cardinality changes break SLI. Mitigation: add synthetic indicator and a metric schema checklist in the PR.
- Ownership drift: owners change without handoff. Mitigation: SLO one-pager must list primary and secondary owners; include in team onboarding.
- False alarms due to traffic spikes: Mitigation: use burn-rate checks and adaptive thresholds for known seasonal events.

Runbook excerpt (quick play):
Trigger: burn rate > 3 for 30m OR SLI drop below target by > 0.5% absolute over 1h
Action 0: Notify on-call (PagerDuty) + create incident ticket with tag slo/<service>
Action 1: Identify root namespace and rollback gating: if a release occurred in the last 15m, consider pause.
Action 2: Switch traffic to previous stable variant or degrade non-critical features behind the path.
Action 3: Communication: CS lead drafts a private customer impact note if top-tier customers are affected.

Facilitator notes and common pitfalls:
- Avoid selecting too many SLIs initially. Start with 1–2 well-understood signals.
- If your SLI uses percentiles, document the aggregation window and ensure the metric exporter uses consistent buckets.
- Don’t conflate SLO target stringency with business priority; you can have a strict SLO for a low-traffic noncritical path only if the cost is justified.
- Keep the first SLO conservative—the objective is to learn measurement gaps and operational overhead.

Follow-up artifacts to produce post-workshop (owner and due date):
- SLO one-pager in confluence (owner: Feature Owner, due: +7 days)
- Dashboard link + screenshot (owner: Observability, due: +10 days)
- Incident playbook stub in Ops repo (owner: SRE, due: +14 days)
- Drill retrospective notes (owner: CS, due: after first drill)

Quick decision matrix (how to pick SLO target):
- If user-facing and high impact: start at 99.9% (7d) then re-evaluate.
- If internal low-impact: 99.0% or instrumented monitor first.
- If metric unstable or sparse: use synthetics for 30-day window, then move to production metric at 60d.

Appendix: quick checklist for feature owners before the workshop:
- Have a list of customer journeys and top 3 failure modes
- Identify the owner who can merge a telemetry PR in the next sprint
- Share sample traffic volumes (p95/p99 request size, QPS)
- Flag any GDPR or PII concerns in telemetry to SRE/security before instrumenting

Notes to self (facilitator):
- Bring two example dashboards to the workshop — one minimal and one with burn-rate.
- Prepare a short demo of the incident workflow (PagerDuty + a dummy ticket).
- Reserve follow-up 30-min slot within 7 days to unblock telemetry PRs.

This playbook is intentionally pragmatic: the emphasis is on getting a measurable SLO into the team’s orbit quickly and then iterating. The first SLO is a learning tool — aim to surface measurement gaps, communication flows, and release controls within the first 60 days.
